title: Szybciej, lepiej, więcej
note: Fenced out of a2_superlatives on purpose (its own note names this exact gap). Adjectives compare with agreement (lepszy/lepsza/lepsze); adverbs compare with ONE fixed word that never changes for gender or number - that is the whole new fact this unit teaches, riding the already-owned naj- prefix rule wholesale. Four families, matching the spine's three named examples (szybko/dobrze/duzo) plus one logged addition: szybko->szybciej->najszybciej is the one genuinely regular pattern (-o adverb -> -iej, k softens to ci - the same softening family the learner has already met in Polak->Polacy from virile_nom, named as a family resemblance, not asserted as one formal rule). dobrze->lepiej->najlepiej and duzo->wiecej->najwiecej are irregular whole forms, but their base adverbs (dobrze, duzo) are already-taught recycled material (a2_smalltalk, a1_gen_endings), so only the comparative/superlative halves are new. mało->mniej->najmniej was added beyond the spine's three examples: its base (mało) is new vocabulary, but it teaches zero new grammar (same rule, same naj- prefix) and was the cleanest way to reach Match's mandatory 12-row board without padding with object-phrase pairs - logged as a scope addition, not a silent guess. niz and od+Gen recycle unchanged from a2_superlatives: od still assigns genitive to the NOUN after it (od brata, od psa - both already taught there), but the adverb itself is invariant either way, which is the direct payoff of 'adverbs never agree.' No new structure risk beyond adverb_comp itself; every noun/verb in example sentences checked individually against the pool before writing (see teaches_lemmas for the four new families; dobrze, duzo, niz, od, brata, psa and every subject noun are pool-legal recycles).

intro.title: The same naj-, on a different kind of word
intro.body:
You already compare adjectives: dobry → lepszy → najlepszy. Those describe NOUNS, and they agree — lepszy, lepsza, lepsze.

Adverbs describe VERBS instead — how you do something, not what a thing is like. They compare the same way, with the same naj- on top for the superlative — but they never agree. One fixed word, always.

dobrze (well) → lepiej (better) → najlepiej (best)
dużo (a lot) → więcej (more) → najwięcej (most)

Mama gotuje lepiej. Tata gotuje lepiej. Dzieci gotują lepiej. — lepiej never changes, no matter who is cooking.
intro.body_pl: Przysłówki: bez końcówek -y/-a/-e. Jedno słowo dla wszystkich.

intro.title: Four families, one pattern
intro.body: szybko → szybciej is the regular one: drop -o, add -iej. dobrze/lepiej and dużo/więcej are irregular whole forms — but you have met their root before: lepiej shares its stem with lepszy, więcej with większy. mało/mniej is new vocabulary, built on the exact same pattern as dużo/więcej — they are opposites, like większy/mniejszy already are.

intro.title: niż and od still work exactly the same
intro.body:
Both ways of saying than still apply, unchanged from najlepszy/od + genitive:

Brat czyta więcej niż ja. — niż leaves the second word alone.
Pracuję więcej od brata. — od still hands the genitive to the NOUN after it (brata, psa — the same forms from od + genitive you already know).

The difference from adjectives: więcej itself never changes shape either way. Only the noun after od ever does.
intro.body_pl: od + dopełniacz (rzeczownik) — przysłówek się nie zmienia.

examples.en: The son reads more than the father.
I work more than the brother.
The father works less than the brother.

quiz.explain: więcej is the comparative of dużo. It never changes for gender — unlike the adjective większy, which would describe a noun instead.
gotuje is a verb, so it takes the adverb lepiej. lepsza/lepszy would describe a noun, not how someone cooks.
lepsza describes kawa, a noun. gotuje is a verb — verbs always take the adverb lepiej, never the adjective form.

quiz.prompt: Ten dom jest większy. On pracuje ___.
quiz.explain: większy describes dom, a noun. pracuje is a verb, so it needs the adverb więcej, which never changes shape.
naj- is the same prefix from najlepszy — it attaches to the comparative szybciej with nothing else changing.
najmniej is naj- + mniej. najmniejszy is the adjective form — it would need a noun to describe.
od still puts brata into the genitive, same as after od + Gen with adjectives — but więcej itself is invariant either way.

type_items.explain: od still hands brat the genitive (brata), exactly as it did with adjectives — więcej itself never changes.
